components.note: 凵 depicts an open container or pit, shown here holding something dangerous inside.
乂 is a crossed mark suggesting something tangled or harmful — trapped inside the container 凵, it gives 凶 its meaning 'vicious, ominous.'
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起凶杀案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ xiōngshā'àn.
example.english: The police are investigating this murder case.
example.fact: DNA fingerprinting was developed by British geneticist Alec Jeffreys in 1984 after he noticed that certain DNA sequences varied enough between individuals to serve as a unique identifier. It was first used to solve a real crime in 1988, when it helped convict Colin Pitchfork of two murders in Leicestershire, England — the first criminal conviction secured through DNA evidence.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 防 is also pronounced fáng, a close match
扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'

example.hanzi: 工人们戴上防护眼镜再开始操作机器。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen dàishàng fánghù yǎnjìng zài kāishǐ cāozuò jīqì.
example.english: The workers put on protective goggles before operating the machinery.
example.fact: Kevlar, now a staple of protective gear like bulletproof vests and cut-resistant gloves, was invented almost by accident in 1965 by DuPont chemist Stephanie Kwolek while she was researching lightweight fibers for tires. Weight for weight, it is about five times stronger than steel.

components.note: 凯 is a simplified form of 凱, whose left side originally pictured a stand holding a large ceremonial drum used to celebrate a military victory.
几 (a small table or stool) sits at the right; combined with the drum imagery it replaced, the character came to mean 'triumphant, victorious.'
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.hanzi: 凯利来自澳大利亚,现在在北京工作。
example.pinyin: Kǎilì láizì Àodàlìyà, xiànzài zài Běijīng gōngzuò.
example.english: Kelly is from Australia and now works in Beijing.
example.fact: Australia's platypus, one of only five living monotreme species, was first described by European naturalists in 1799 — who initially suspected the specimen was a hoax, an animal stitched together from parts of a duck and a mammal, since no such creature was known to lay eggs while also producing milk.

components.note: 冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.
口 (mouth), stacked three times — many mouths talking about or judging something, the source of 品's meaning 'product, item; quality, rank.'

example.hanzi: 这家商店卖各种各样的商品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn mài gèzhǒng gèyàng de shāngpǐn.
example.english: This store sells all kinds of merchandise.
example.fact: The Dutch tulip mania of 1637 is often cited as the world's first recorded speculative economic bubble: at its peak, single rare tulip bulbs traded for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman, before prices collapsed within weeks.

meanings: variant of 反覆|反复[fan3 fu4]

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 反 pictures pushing against a steep surface.
又 (a hand) — a hand pushing back against a cliff gave 反 its meaning 'to turn over' or 'opposite.'
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'

example.hanzi: 他反复练习这首曲子,直到弹得完美。
example.pinyin: Tā fǎnfù liànxí zhè shǒu qǔzi, zhídào tán de wánměi.
example.english: He practiced this piece of music repeatedly until he could play it perfectly.
example.fact: In 1885, German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus published the 'forgetting curve,' showing that newly learned information fades rapidly within days unless it is deliberately reviewed — a finding that still underlies modern spaced-repetition study techniques.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 波 refers to waves on water
皮 (pí) gives a sound close to 波's reading bō, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 工程师用波特率来衡量数据传输的速度。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī yòng bōtèlǜ lái héngliáng shùjù chuánshū de sùdù.
example.english: Engineers use baud rate to measure the speed of data transmission.
example.fact: The baud, a unit measuring signal changes per second in telecommunications, is named after Émile Baudot, a French engineer who invented an early digital telegraph code in the 1870s that let multiple messages share a single telegraph line.

meanings: to get hit by a bullet

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
弓 (bow) — 弹 relates to a projectile shot from a bow, like a pellet
单 (dān) gives a loose sound connection to 弹's reading dàn

example.hanzi: 那名士兵在战斗中中弹受伤。
example.pinyin: Nà míng shìbīng zài zhàndòu zhōng zhòngdàn shòushāng.
example.english: That soldier was hit by a bullet and wounded in the battle.
example.fact: A bullet fired from an AK-47 travels at roughly 715 meters per second, more than twice the speed of sound. That is why a supersonic bullet passing overhead produces a sharp crack that reaches an observer's ear before the sound of the gunshot itself.

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
亻 depicts a standing person.
匕 depicts the same person turned upside down — the shift from one posture to the other gave 化 its meaning 'to change, to transform.'

example.hanzi: 她大学时主修生化专业。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué shí zhǔxiū shēnghuà zhuānyè.
example.english: She majored in biochemistry in college.
example.fact: The double-helix structure of DNA, announced by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, relied heavily on X-ray diffraction images produced by chemist Rosalind Franklin, whose crucial contribution went largely unrecognized during her lifetime.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 债 concerns something a person owes.
责 (duty, responsibility) — an obligation owed to someone else, together giving 债 its meaning 'debt, loan.'
力 (strength, effort) sits at the base — 务 relates to tasks that require exertion, giving its meaning 'affairs, business.'
The compressed strokes above derive from 敄, the phonetic element in the traditional form 務, whose sound is close in origin to wù.

example.hanzi: 这个国家背负着巨额债务。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā bèifù zhe jù'é zhàiwù.
example.english: This country is carrying a huge amount of debt.
example.fact: The earliest known written debt records are Mesopotamian clay tablets dating back roughly 5,000 years, which recorded loans of grain, silver, and livestock between merchants — making debt one of the oldest documented human institutions.

components.note: 余 originally pictured a simple thatched hut or shelter. The character was later borrowed for its sound to write the unrelated words 'surplus, remainder' and the literary pronoun 'I.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 这个计划安排得很紧,没有留下失败的余地。
example.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà ānpái de hěn jǐn, méiyǒu liú xià shībài de yúdì.
example.english: This plan is scheduled so tightly that it leaves no room for failure.
example.fact: The Brooklyn Bridge, completed in 1883, was built with roughly six times the strength its engineers calculated it would ever need — a wide safety margin that chief engineer Washington Roebling insisted on after discovering a supplier had sold the project substandard cable wire.

meanings: to be later than the time stipulated or agreed upon

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 这种手机型号已经过时了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shǒujī xínghào yǐjīng guòshí le.
example.english: This model of phone is already out of date.
example.fact: The original iPhone, released in 2007, shipped with just 128 megabytes of RAM — less memory than many basic smartwatches carry today, a reminder of how quickly computing hardware becomes obsolete.

components.note: A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'
段 shows 殳 (a hand wielding a tool) cutting or shaping stone into pieces — giving 段 its meaning 'section, segment, paragraph.'

example.hanzi: 我只记得那部电影的几个片段。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ jìde nà bù diànyǐng de jǐ gè piànduàn.
example.english: I only remember a few fragments of that movie.
example.fact: Almost all of the ancient Greek poet Sappho's work survives only in fragments, preserved mostly on scraps of papyrus recovered from Egyptian rubbish heaps; new fragments of her poetry are still occasionally discovered, including a significant find published in 2014.

meanings: erhua variant of 大伙[da4 huo3]

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 大伙儿一起去爬山吧。
example.pinyin: Dàhuǒr yīqǐ qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's all go hiking together.
example.fact: Emperor penguins survive Antarctic winters by huddling together in groups of thousands, and individuals continually rotate position so that everyone takes a turn standing in the warmer center of the huddle rather than the colder outer edge.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 滑 describes something as slick or slippery, like a wet surface.
骨 (gǔ) is only distantly related in sound to huá — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
木 (wood) — boards and planks like 板 are traditionally made of wood.
反 (fǎn) gives a rhyme close to bǎn, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在公园里玩滑板。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài gōngyuán lǐ wán huábǎn.
example.english: He likes skateboarding in the park.
example.fact: Skateboards were invented by California surfers in the 1950s who wanted a way to practice their sport on land. The sport was transformed in the early 1970s when Frank Nasworthy introduced polyurethane wheels, which gripped the pavement far better than the clay wheels used before.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 本案将由三名法官共同审理。
example.pinyin: Běn'àn jiāng yóu sān míng fǎguān gòngtóng shěnlǐ.
example.english: This case will be jointly tried by three judges.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials of 1945–46 established a lasting precedent for prosecuting crimes against humanity, with judges from four different Allied nations — the US, UK, France, and the Soviet Union — sitting together on the same bench to hear evidence.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.
宀 (a roof) sets the scene inside a household.
丰 pictures a sharp implement piercing downward — an injury done under one's own roof, giving 害 its meaning 'harm, injury.'

example.hanzi: 被害人是一名年轻女子。
example.pinyin: Bèihàirén shì yī míng niánqīng nǚzǐ.
example.english: The victim was a young woman.
example.fact: Forensic entomologists can estimate how long a body has been deceased by studying blowfly activity: blowflies typically lay eggs on remains within minutes of death, and the developmental stage of the resulting larvae provides a reliable biological clock.

components.note: 页 (head) — 预 relates to looking ahead or foreseeing beforehand
予 (yǔ) gives a sound close to 预's reading yù, differing mainly in tone
讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 专家预计明年经济会有所增长。
example.pinyin: Zhuānjiā yùjì míngnián jīngjì huì yǒu suǒ zēngzhǎng.
example.english: Experts forecast that the economy will grow somewhat next year.
example.fact: Weather forecasting accuracy has improved so dramatically that a modern five-day forecast is now about as reliable as a one-day forecast was in the 1980s, thanks to satellite data, ocean buoys, and vastly greater computing power.

components.note: ⺺ — an abstract mark meant to depict strokes made by a writing brush, the origin of 书's meaning 'book, document, letter.'
广 (shelter/building) — 店 names a building used for business.
占 (zhàn) gives a sound distantly related to diàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 巷子拐角有一家小书店。
example.pinyin: Xiàngzi guǎijiǎo yǒu yī jiā xiǎo shūdiàn.
example.english: There is a small bookstore at the corner of the alley.
example.fact: Shakespeare and Company, an English-language bookstore founded in Paris in 1919, became a gathering place for expatriate writers such as Ernest Hemingway and F. Scott Fitzgerald, who sometimes borrowed money or slept there when they were broke.

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'

example.hanzi: 同事们午休时说笑聊天,气氛很轻松。
example.pinyin: Tóngshìmen wǔxiū shí shuōxiào liáotiān, qìfēn hěn qīngsōng.
example.english: Colleagues chat and joke during their lunch break, keeping the mood relaxed.
example.fact: Laughter is highly contagious: studies of social behavior find people are roughly thirty times more likely to laugh when they are with others than when they are alone, which is one reason sitcoms use a laugh track.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain was one of the first things ancient people owned and kept for themselves.
厶 pictures something folded in on itself and hidden away, giving 私 its sense of 'private, personal, one's own.'
事 pictures a hand 又 grasping a forked staff or tally once used by an official to record matters — the origin of its meaning 'affair, matter; to attend to.'

example.hanzi: 这是我的私事,请不要过问。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de sīshì, qǐng bùyào guòwèn.
example.english: This is my personal matter, please don't ask about it.
example.fact: The modern legal concept of a 'right to privacy' traces largely to an 1890 Harvard Law Review article by Samuel Warren and Louis Brandeis, written partly in response to intrusive newspaper photography made possible by the newly portable handheld camera.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洞 originally described water hollowing out a cave or hole in rock.
同 (tóng) gives a sound distantly related to dòng, having drifted apart over time.
穴 pictures the mouth of a cave, with a peaked roof and an opening below — the image behind its meaning 'cave, den.'

example.hanzi: 考古学家在洞穴里发现了古代壁画。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài dòngxué lǐ fāxiàn le gǔdài bìhuà.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered ancient cave paintings inside the cave.
example.fact: The Lascaux cave in southwestern France, discovered in 1940 by four teenagers chasing their dog into a hole in the ground, contains paintings of horses, bulls, and deer estimated to be around 17,000 years old.

meanings: to go on an official or business trip

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
羊 (sheep) — work involving livestock, done imperfectly
工 (work) — the labor itself, linked to the idea of falling short

example.hanzi: 他下周要去上海出差。
example.pinyin: Tā xià zhōu yào qù Shànghǎi chūchāi.
example.english: He is going on a business trip to Shanghai next week.
example.fact: A traveler's circadian clock generally needs about one full day to adjust for every time zone crossed, which is why crossing several zones on a business trip often produces jet lag that lingers for nearly a week.

meanings: to carry on a clandestine love affair

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这部小说描写了一段偷情的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù xiǎoshuō miáoxiě le yī duàn tōuqíng de gùshì.
example.english: This novel depicts a story of a clandestine love affair.
example.fact: Leo Tolstoy's 1877 novel Anna Karenina, built around its heroine's affair, opens with one of the most quoted lines in world literature — 'All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way' — a line Tolstoy is said to have revised many times before publication.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/place) — reflects 阿's original meaning related to a hill or slope
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 阿's reading ā
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.

example.hanzi: 在伊斯兰教中,信徒尊称真主为阿拉。
example.pinyin: Zài Yīsīlán jiào zhōng, xìntú zūnchēng zhēnzhǔ wéi Ālā.
example.english: In Islam, believers respectfully refer to God as Allah.
example.fact: During the Hajj pilgrimage, Muslims circle the Kaaba in Mecca seven times in a counterclockwise direction, a ritual called tawaf that is believed to date back to the time of the prophet Abraham.

components.note: 手 (hand) — 摩 describes rubbing something with the hand.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support

example.hanzi: 他每天骑摩托车去上班。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān qí mótuōchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: He rides a motorcycle to work every day.
example.fact: The first motorcycle, Gottlieb Daimler's 'Reitwagen,' was built in Germany in 1885. It had a wooden frame, iron-banded wheels, and no suspension, and was designed mainly as a test bed for Daimler's new gasoline engine rather than as practical transportation.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — suggests a gesture, a beckoning motion.
召 depicts a call or summons — a hand gesture calling someone over gave 招 its meaning 'to beckon, to recruit.'
亻 (person) — the one making an offering.
共 (together/both hands) — a person offering something with both hands gave 供 its meaning 'to supply, provide, offer.'

example.hanzi: 嫌疑人最终向警方招供了。
example.pinyin: Xiányírén zuìzhōng xiàng jǐngfāng zhāogòng le.
example.english: The suspect finally confessed to the police.
example.fact: The Reid Technique, a widely used American interrogation method developed in the 1940s and 1950s, has been criticized by psychologists for sometimes producing false confessions; researchers studying wrongful convictions later overturned by DNA evidence found false confessions were a contributing factor in a notable share of those cases.

components.note: 羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'

example.hanzi: 这支笔只要五十美分。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī bǐ zhǐyào wǔshí Měifēn.
example.english: This pen costs only fifty cents.
example.fact: The United States Mint has reported that producing a single one-cent coin costs more than two cents in metal and manufacturing expenses, meaning the US government loses money every time it makes a penny.

components.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
彳 (to walk) — a person moving, sent somewhere to work.
殳 (a tool held in the hand) — carrying out labor, together giving 役 its meaning 'service, forced labor.'

example.hanzi: 他二十岁开始服役。
example.pinyin: Tā èrshí suì kāishǐ fúyì.
example.english: He began his military service at age twenty.
example.fact: Switzerland maintains a militia-based army in which most male citizens complete mandatory service and then keep their government-issued rifle at home between periodic refresher trainings, a long-standing feature of the country's policy of armed neutrality.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.
关 is a simplified form of 關, which pictured a wooden crossbar or latch bolted across a gate 門 to shut it — the source of 关's meaning 'to close, to shut' and by extension 'to relate to, to concern.'
糸 (thread/silk) — 系 relates to connecting or tying things together, like threads linking into a system.

example.hanzi: 婚前性关系在某些文化中仍被视为禁忌。
example.pinyin: Hūnqián xìngguānxi zài mǒu xiē wénhuà zhōng réng bèi shìwéi jìnjì.
example.english: Premarital sexual relations are still considered taboo in some cultures.
example.fact: Alfred Kinsey's 1948 and 1953 reports on human sexual behavior were among the first large-scale scientific surveys of the topic, drawing on thousands of personal interviews and challenging many assumptions widely held at the time.

meanings: to get off or out of

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 请在下一站下车。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài xià yī zhàn xiàchē.
example.english: Please get off at the next stop.
example.fact: The Brazilian city of Curitiba pioneered the modern 'bus rapid transit' system in the 1970s, using tube-shaped stations where passengers pay their fare before boarding — a design that sped up loading dramatically and has since been copied by cities around the world.

components.note: 戈 (a spear) in the center is the weapon being wielded.
廾 (two hands) surrounding it show hands gripping the weapon on guard, giving 戒 its meaning 'to guard against, to warn.'
龶 depicts a poisonous plant, tying 毒 to its meaning 'poison.'
母 (mǔ) gives a rhyme close to dú, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 他进入戒毒中心接受治疗。
example.pinyin: Tā jìnrù jièdú zhōngxīn jiēshòu zhìliáo.
example.english: He entered a rehab center for treatment.
example.fact: Methadone maintenance therapy, developed in the 1960s by researchers Vincent Dole and Marie Nyswander, was one of the first medical treatments shown to reduce opioid cravings and withdrawal symptoms without producing the same intense high.

components.note: 宣 depicts a grand hall (宀) with an open, radiating space inside, evoking a palace where proclamations were made.
禾 (grain) — 称 originally described weighing grain on a scale.
The remaining strokes derive from 爯, a hand lifting a weight in the traditional form 稱, whose sound is close in origin to chēng.

example.hanzi: 这家公司宣称新产品完全环保。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī xuānchēng xīn chǎnpǐn wánquán huánbǎo.
example.english: This company claims its new product is completely eco-friendly.
example.fact: The term 'greenwashing' was coined in 1986 by environmentalist Jay Westerveld after he noticed hotels asking guests to reuse towels to 'save the environment' while doing comparatively little to reduce their actual environmental impact elsewhere.

components.note: 自 here depicts a head (the character also independently means 'nose, self').
丷 depicts hair atop the head — 首 originally pictured a head with hair, giving its meaning 'head, chief, first.'
页 (head) — relates to 领's meaning 'neck, collar; to lead,' the head/neck area.
令 (lìng) gives a sound hint — 领 is pronounced lǐng, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 部落首领带领族人迁移到新的土地。
example.pinyin: Bùluò shǒulǐng dàilǐng zúrén qiānyí dào xīn de tǔdì.
example.english: The tribal chief led his people to migrate to new land.
example.fact: Anthropological studies of many hunter-gatherer societies have found that leadership was often situational and non-hereditary, chosen for a specific task like a hunt or a journey, rather than fixed in a permanent chief as once commonly assumed.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 请's meaning 'to request, invite; please,' a spoken request.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 请 is pronounced qǐng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
宀 (roof) — represents a home.
各 (each, various) — a person arriving from elsewhere and welcomed under one's roof gave 客 its meaning 'guest, visitor.'

example.hanzi: 今天我请客,大家随便点。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒ qǐngkè, dàjiā suíbiàn diǎn.
example.english: I'm treating everyone today, order whatever you like.
example.fact: In his influential 1925 study 'The Gift,' anthropologist Marcel Mauss argued that gift-giving and hospitality across widely different cultures follow a similar hidden rule: receiving something, even a shared meal, quietly creates a social obligation to reciprocate later.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — fighting back with bare hands
亢 — the throat, a vulnerable point defended while resisting
扌 (hand) — 拒 describes pushing something away with the hand, refusing.
巨 (jù) is an exact match for the sound of 拒.

example.hanzi: 他极力抗拒改变旧习惯。
example.pinyin: Tā jílì kàngjù gǎibiàn jiù xíguàn.
example.english: He strongly resists changing his old habits.
example.fact: Habitual behaviors are encoded largely in a brain region called the basal ganglia, which forms efficient neural pathways through repetition — part of why long-standing habits can feel almost automatic and are resistant to conscious change.

meanings: fig. way out of an embarrassing situation

components.note: 台 originally pictured a raised earthen platform or mound — the source of its meaning 'platform, stage, terrace.'
阝 (hill) — 阶 originally referred to steps built into a hillside or mound
介 (jiè) gives a sound close to 阶's reading jiē, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 老人小心地走下台阶。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén xiǎoxīn de zǒu xià táijiē.
example.english: The old man carefully walked down the steps.
example.fact: The Spanish Steps in Rome, built between 1723 and 1725, consist of 135 steps connecting the Piazza di Spagna at the bottom to the church of Trinità dei Monti at the top, and remain one of the city's most famous meeting spots.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
亻 (person) — the one making an offering.
共 (together/both hands) — a person offering something with both hands gave 供 its meaning 'to supply, provide, offer.'

example.hanzi: 警方记录了目击者的口供。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng jìlù le mùjīzhě de kǒugòng.
example.english: The police recorded the eyewitness's oral statement.
example.fact: Cognitive psychologist Elizabeth Loftus's research beginning in the 1970s showed that eyewitness memory can be distorted by suggestive questioning after the fact, a finding that has since contributed to reforms in how police interview witnesses.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 演 originally described water flowing and spreading out, later extended to 'developing, unfolding'
寅 (yín) gives a sound distantly related to 演's reading yǎn, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō

example.hanzi: 他在毕业典礼上发表了演说。
example.pinyin: Tā zài bìyè diǎnlǐ shàng fābiǎo le yǎnshuō.
example.english: He delivered a speech at the graduation ceremony.
example.fact: Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech, delivered on August 28, 1963, at the March on Washington, was partly improvised — the famous refrain wasn't part of his prepared remarks and was added spontaneously as he spoke.

components.note: 巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.
方 (a flag/banner) — a shared banner under which a group gathers.
矢 (arrow) — warriors bound by oath under one flag gave 族 its meaning 'clan, ethnic group, tribe.'

example.hanzi: 中国是一个多民族国家。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó shì yī gè duō mínzú guójiā.
example.english: China is a multi-ethnic country.
example.fact: Papua New Guinea, with a population of roughly 10 million people, is home to more than 800 distinct languages, making it by far the most linguistically diverse country on Earth relative to its size.

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'
方 is thought to depict either a two-handled plow or a squared corner post; its exact ancient picture is debated, but it came to mean 'square, direction, method.'

example.hanzi: 这种建筑风格受到西方文化的影响。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng jiànzhù fēnggé shòudào Xīfāng wénhuà de yǐngxiǎng.
example.english: This architectural style is influenced by Western culture.
example.fact: For more than 1,500 years starting around the 2nd century BC, the Silk Road network of trade routes carried not just goods like silk and spices but also architectural styles, religions, and technologies back and forth between East and West.

components.note: 囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
阝 (a mound/wall) — 防 relates to defensive walls and prevention
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 防 is also pronounced fáng, a close match
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).

example.hanzi: 国防部宣布了新的军事预算。
example.pinyin: Guófángbù xuānbù le xīn de jūnshì yùsuàn.
example.english: The Defense Department announced a new military budget.
example.fact: The Pentagon, headquarters of the US Department of Defense, was built in just sixteen months and completed in 1943. Despite being one of the largest office buildings in the world by floor area, its five-sided ring design means any two points inside are no more than a seven-minute walk apart.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.
人 (person), tripled — three people together depict a crowd, giving 众 its meaning 'many, multitude.'

example.hanzi: 演讲结束后,听众热烈鼓掌。
example.pinyin: Yǎnjiǎng jiéshù hòu, tīngzhòng rèliè gǔzhǎng.
example.english: After the speech ended, the audience applauded warmly.
example.fact: Orson Welles's 1938 radio adaptation of 'The War of the Worlds' famously led some listeners to briefly believe a real Martian invasion was underway, though historians have since shown that contemporary newspapers considerably exaggerated the scale of the panic.

components.note: 攵 (to strike, to act) — 赦 (to pardon) is framed as an authoritative act.
赤 (chì) gives a sound only distantly related to shè today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
免 originally pictured a person wearing a cap or mask, related to 冕 (ceremonial crown); the image of removing such a covering gave 免 its meaning 'to avoid, to be exempt from.'

example.hanzi: 总统决定赦免这名囚犯。
example.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng juédìng shèmiǎn zhè míng qiúfàn.
example.english: The president decided to pardon this prisoner.
example.fact: The US Constitution grants the president broad power to pardon federal offenses. One of the most controversial uses of that power was President Gerald Ford's 1974 pardon of Richard Nixon, issued before Nixon had been formally charged with any crime.

components.note: 龶-shaped top pictures a ripe stalk of grain.
夂 below pictures roots or a foot, together giving 麦 its meaning 'wheat.'
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 早餐我喜欢吃一碗麦片。
example.pinyin: Zǎocān wǒ xǐhuan chī yī wǎn màipiàn.
example.english: I like to eat a bowl of oatmeal for breakfast.
example.fact: Oats are unusually rich in a soluble fiber called beta-glucan, which clinical studies have shown can help lower LDL cholesterol — evidence strong enough that the US FDA has allowed heart-health claims on oat products since 1997.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — a form of 肉 (flesh, body), marking the character as related to a body part or bodily substance.
力 (lì) gives a sound close to 肋's reading lē, sharing the same initial consonant.
冎 pictures a joint of bone.
⺼ (flesh) sits below, together giving 骨 its meaning 'bone.'

example.hanzi: 他摔倒时摔断了两根肋骨。
example.pinyin: Tā shuāidǎo shí shuāiduàn le liǎng gēn lèigǔ.
example.english: He broke two ribs when he fell.
example.fact: Most people are born with 12 pairs of ribs, but roughly 1 in 200 people has an extra rib near the neck, called a cervical rib, which is usually harmless but can occasionally press on nearby nerves or blood vessels.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — bells are made of metal.
令 (lìng) gives the sound — a close match for líng, differing only in tone.
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 手机的铃声突然响了起来。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī de língshēng tūrán xiǎng le qǐlái.
example.english: The phone's ringtone suddenly rang.
example.fact: Nokia's iconic default ringtone, the 'Nokia Tune,' is adapted from a passage of 'Gran Vals,' a nineteenth-century classical guitar piece by Spanish composer Francisco Tárrega, and became one of the most-heard melodies in the world during mobile phones' peak popularity in the 2000s.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body
却 (què) gives a sound distantly related to 脚's reading jiǎo, having drifted apart over time
止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'

example.hanzi: 楼梯上传来沉重的脚步声。
example.pinyin: Lóutī shàng chuánlái chénzhòng de jiǎobù shēng.
example.english: Heavy footsteps could be heard on the stairs.
example.fact: Because each person's stride length, foot angle, and weight distribution form a distinctive pattern, forensic gait analysis can sometimes help identify individuals from CCTV footage of nothing more than their footsteps.

components.note: 儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.
艹 (grass, plant) — 芒 names the pointed tip of a grass or grain.
亡 (wáng) gives a sound close to máng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 太阳的光芒照耀着大地。
example.pinyin: Tàiyáng de guāngmáng zhàoyào zhe dàdì.
example.english: The sun's rays shine down on the earth.
example.fact: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel the roughly 150 million kilometers from the Sun's surface to Earth, meaning we always see the Sun slightly as it looked a few minutes in the past.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
关 is a simplified form of 關, which pictured a wooden crossbar or latch bolted across a gate 門 to shut it — the source of 关's meaning 'to close, to shut' and by extension 'to relate to, to concern.'

example.hanzi: 公司正在努力度过这个难关。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèngzài nǔlì dùguò zhège nánguān.
example.english: The company is working hard to get through this difficult period.
example.fact: After a devastating 1985 earthquake, Mexico City built one of the world's first citywide seismic early-warning systems, using sensors near the Pacific coast that can give residents up to about 60 seconds of warning before shaking from a major quake arrives.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 司机在路口掉头。
example.pinyin: Sījī zài lùkǒu diàotóu.
example.english: The driver made a U-turn at the intersection.
example.fact: So-called 'Michigan lefts,' designed in the 1960s, route drivers past their intended left turn to make a U-turn at a median crossover instead of turning directly across oncoming traffic — a design shown in later studies to meaningfully reduce crashes at busy intersections.
